chunks: Muʿammar ibn Khallād narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:
When he was in Khurāsān, after performing the Fajr prayer, he would sit in his place of salat until the sun rose.
Then a pouch containing siwāks would be brought to him, and he would use them one by one.
Then frankincense would be brought to him, and he would chew it, then leave that aside.
Then the muṣḥaf would be brought to him, and he would read from it.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose rising marked the end of his sitting period
key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: the dawn prayer time, referring here to the Fajr prayer
key_terms.الْمُصْحَفِ: the written copy of the Qur'an from which he recited
key_terms.خَرِيطَةٍ: a pouch or small bag brought containing siwāks
key_terms.مَسَاوِيكُ: tooth-cleaning sticks used for oral hygiene and sunnah practice
key_terms.مُصَلَّاهُ: his place of salat, where he remained after prayer

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام do after the Fajr prayer in Khurāsān?
ai.summary: This hadith describes part of the morning routine of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام in Khurāsān after the Fajr prayer. It highlights remaining in the place of worship after dawn, using the siwāk, and reciting from the Qur'an, reflecting devotional discipline and refined religious conduct.
